maternal conditions (asthma, diabetes, obesity, poor oral health, thyroid disease, chronic cardiac or kidney disease); pregnancy complications (gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders); infections (GBS, chorioamnionitis, UTI, HIV, hepatitis B, STIs, toxoplasmosis, CMV); prenatal diagnoses and interventions; maternal medications and supplements; tobacco, alcohol or drug use; prior adverse pregnancy outcome.

mother's hepatitis B, HIV, GBS, blood group and Rh status; preterm labor or premature rupture of membranes; mode of delivery and instrumentation; medications and anesthesia; episiotomy or lacerations; duration of labor; complications (fever, infection, bleeding, preeclampsia incl. HELLP).

fetal distress; IUGR, macrosomia, birth trauma; gestational age, birth weight and Apgar score; transition problems (respiratory distress, cyanosis, hypoglycemia, poor feeding, temperature instability, jitteriness, lethargy); risk of withdrawal from maternal substance use; vitamin K and eye prophylaxis.

newborn blood type and direct Coombs; vital signs; blood sugar if at risk; weight loss or gain; feeding (LATCH scores, frequency, duration; formula type if not breastfeeding); sleep-wake pattern; meconium passage and wet diapers; risk of severe jaundice; anomalies suggesting a need for genetic evaluation.
a comprehensive family history is recommended at the 1 month visit.

head shape; eye discharge; ears, nose and throat; breathing; vomiting or spitting, bowel movements, umbilical stump; genitals or rectum; skin; development (muscle strength, movement of arms or legs, developmental concerns).
